drills.q: Run the decision tree on 'blockchain supply-chain traceability' vendor pitch.
drills.a: Who writes? If one company owns the system of record -> database+API. Suppliers verifying without trusting you -> public hash anchoring (read-only verification needs no shared ledger). Multiple distrusting writers with no acceptable operator AND neutral execution needed -> public chain first, permissioned second. Then price integration + key mgmt + year-ten funding.

drills.q: Why did TradeLens fail despite Maersk scale and IBM backing?
drills.a: Competitors wouldn't route critical workflows through rival-influenceable infrastructure; adoption stayed thin beyond Maersk while IBM carried costs. Benefits never beat EDI+email because the trust problem was smaller than assumed - DCSA standards took the messaging role. Wound down late 2022 into early 2023.

drills.q: ASX CHESS DLT cancellation (~A$250M): the transferable lesson?
drills.a: ASX kept itself as SINGLE operator so decentralization was decorative while adding novel failure modes and years of delay. When the operator is trusted by construction (licensed market utility), DLT buys nothing - honest project is boring modernization. Cancelled Nov 2022. Evaluate architecture-category fit BEFORE technology.

drills.q: GDPR vs immutable ledger: design patterns that reconcile them.
drills.a: PII never on-chain - hashed personal data is still personal data (EDPB). Patterns: PII off-chain in erasable storage with commitments/references on-chain; crypto-shredding = client-side encryption + key destruction for erasure. Design erasure pre-launch; retrofitting immutability is impossible by definition.

drills.q: When is permissioned chain genuinely right over public? Preconditions.
drills.a: All must hold: bounded identified membership (regulated institutions); validator funding committed long-term; confidentiality beyond what public+ZK offers today; regulatory constraints on public settlement. Kinexys fits (known banks, funded infra, ~$2B/day interbank deposits). Otherwise public L1/L2 + compliance wrappers wins.

drills.q: Why did stablecoins succeed where trade-finance consortia died?
drills.a: Stablecoins serve strangers globally with 24/7 neutrality: holders needn't trust a consortium, just regulated issuers (GENIUS Act reserves, July 2025). Organic demand (dollar access, settlement speed), self-onboarding wallets, no competitor-cooperation requirement. Consortia inverted incentives: rivals funding shared infra for marginal gains.

drills.q: Design the compliance stack for a tokenized fund on public chains.
drills.a: Transfer restrictions in token contract enforced between allowlisted KYC'd wallets (transfer agent), continuous sanctions re-screening, travel-rule data off-chain, freeze/recover roles for court orders held by regulated parties, chain-analytics surveillance hooks. BUIDL shape: SEC-registered wrapper + permissioned transfers + public settlement. Tradeoff admitted: composability shrinks to approved venues.

drills.q: Auditors want tamper-evident internal trade logs. Blockchain? Design the alternative.
drills.a: No: append-only DB with hash chaining, Merkle roots published daily to EXTERNAL anchors (public-chain tx, notary API) - CT-log generalized. Auditors verify any entry against any day's root without trusting your storage; retroactive edits break all future proofs. Doesn't cover: counterparties WRITING shared state, or you colluding with the anchor at publication time (cross-anchor to two points).

drills.q: Leadership wants 'a blockchain strategy'. What do you deliver instead?
drills.a: Decision memo: use-cases run through the tree (most die Q1/Q2), 1-2 narrow pilots with measured ROI (stablecoin vendor payments FX savings; anchored audit logs for one regulator flow), explicit non-goals, cost envelope including key management, kill-criteria per pilot. Options with prices, not platform choices - reframes blocker as architect.
